ground_truth_root_cause: The upstream third-party forex API provider (fxrates-api) exhausted the currency-service API rate limit quota. Logs show X-RateLimit-Remaining dropping to 0 at 2026-05-13T11:49:22Z, followed by repeated HTTP 429 responses from fxrates-api. currency-service propagated 503 errors to checkout-service, triggering its circuit breaker to open after 3 consecutive failures at 2026-05-13T11:49:49Z. No recent deploy SHA is directly responsible; the rate limit was hit due to elevated call volume against a fixed quota cap on the fxrates-api subscription tier. The currency-service itself is operationally healthy. The root cause is the external fxrates-api dependency being rate-limited.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: Instruct the currency-service team to relax the stale cache rejection threshold (increase max_allowed_age from 300s to 900s) to allow serving cached FX rates while the quota resets. 2. Wait for the fxrates-api quota reset at approximately 2026-05-13T11:55:20Z or switch to a pre-configured backup forex provider. 3. Once currency-service health endpoint returns OK, manually reset the checkout-service circuit breaker or wait for the 60s retry window to expire. 4. Long-term: upgrade the fxrates-api subscription tier and implement proactive rate-limit throttling in currency-service. Estimated time to restore service: 15-20 minutes.
